solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Over route limit? Could be a hidden reason

indicators.note: Could be says the preceding letters might, once rearranged, be something else

explanation.surface: A query about a speed or distance limit on a road, then a hint that some secret motive lies behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' is the anagram signal, applied to all fourteen letters of 'Over route limit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealed purpose behind an action is exactly what the phrase means: a motive kept out of sight.

clue.text: Swing net with no difficulty they say

parts.note: a net is a trap

indicators.note: they say signals that a word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: doing something with ease means with no difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone claims a mesh hammock swings effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' gives EZE, how EASE is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus artist's bar hung on ropes is a kind of swing used high above a safety net.

clue.text: Rule out government control

indicators.note: out says the letter for government is dropped

parts.note: a monarch's reign is their rule

explanation.surface: Banning government control by decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something in check, as with a horse's strap, is to hold it under control.

clue.text: Gall present in two trees

parts.note: the growth is found on an oak, and its name joins two tree names

explanation.surface: A growth found on two trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is two trees, oak and apple, but it grows only on one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A round growth that forms on oak leaves and twigs, caused by a wasp larva, is this kind of gall.

clue.text: Student doctor cut back to front in a very short time

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside the short spell of time

parts.note: mo is short for a moment

indicators.note: back to front moves the final letter of the word for cut round to the start

parts.note: to dice food is to cut it into cubes

explanation.surface: A trainee doctor makes a cut almost backwards in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' shifts E from the end of DICE to give EDIC, which goes 'in' MO.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a doctor or a medical student, from Italian.

clue.text: Broken icy earth covers heart of Kansas. These might help to get a grip

definitions.text: These might help to get a grip

indicators.note: Broken says these letters are smashed and remade
heart of picks the middle letters of the state name

explanation.surface: Cracked frozen ground lies over the centre of Kansas; something may help grip it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges ICY EARTH, which 'covers' NS, the 'heart of' Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal chains fitted to car wheels give traction on snow and ice, helping the wheels to grip.

clue.text: Thrilling sensation cut short by angry outburst

indicators.note: cut short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a vibe is a feeling or sensation
a rant is an angry outburst

explanation.surface: An exciting feeling ended abruptly by a tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the E of VIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of energy and life is exciting, and in that sense thrilling.

clue.text: Like a lemon dessert?

parts.note: lemon is sour and a pudding is sugary, so a lemon pudding is both at once

explanation.surface: Describing the taste of a lemon pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasting both sharp and sugary at once, or pleasant mixed with sad, is what the word describes.

clue.text: Arrested, at first the old man got in a tizz

indicators.note: at first places the old man's letters before the word for arrested

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father, one's old man
nicked is British slang for arrested by the police

explanation.surface: A father, just arrested, flaps and loses composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' tells you to put PA ahead of NICKED, though it reads as 'initially, when arrested'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get in a tizz is to become flustered and alarmed, a state of sudden fear and panic.

clue.text: Doctor of Law's endless talk

indicators.note: endless says the word for talk loses its final letter

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for talk on and on, as in 'rabbit on'

explanation.surface: A legal scholar is noted for never stopping talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the last T from RABBIT; 'rabbit' meaning chatter is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher is a scholar of Jewish law, so the title fits a doctor of that law.

clue.text: One may be spoiling to take the gilt off it

definitions.text: One may be spoiling to take the gilt off it

parts.words: One may be spoiling to take the gilt off it
parts.note: the idiom 'take the gilt off' means to spoil something pleasant

explanation.surface: Someone eager to ruin a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To take the gilt off the ... ' is an idiom for spoiling something; gilded ginger cakes were sold at old fairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a spiced cake that was once decorated with gold leaf at fairs.

clue.text: Day in Rome — departs Italy heading west

indicators.note: heading west moves the letter for Italy towards the left, the start of the word in an across entry

parts.note: dies, as in departs this life
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A traveller in Rome notes the day they leave Italy, going west.
explanation.walkthrough: DIES (departs this life) has its I shifted to the front by 'heading west', giving the Roman date.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient Roman calendar the Ides was a particular day of each month, the 15th or 13th.

clue.text: Challenger perhaps accepts fair blows if one's knocked out

indicators.note: blows here means is blown apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
knocked out says the letter for one is removed from the letters before they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boxing challenger takes punches fairly, even after one of them flattens him.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I ('one') from ACCEPTS FAIR and rearrange ('blows') the rest. Challenger was a NASA space shuttle, not a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Challenger was a space shuttle, one example of a vehicle built to travel beyond the atmosphere.

clue.text: Suspicious incident involving time and money leads to accusation

indicators.note: involving puts the rearranged letters around the two letters
Suspicious says the letters are fishy and need rearranging

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for money, as in economics

explanation.surface: A dubious event concerning time and cash leads to a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspicious' gives the anagram, INDICENT, which goes round T and M as 'involving' says; 'leads to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal charge of a serious crime is a legal accusation.

clue.text: What a pest! Jealous and cunning

parts.note: green with envy, so green means jealous
fly is British slang for sharp and cunning

explanation.surface: An exclamation about someone envious and sly, a real nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are a garden pest, the green species being a gardener's scourge on roses.

clue.text: Gene's fine performance of Romeo

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
an act is a performance
o' is a shortened of, as in o'clock
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Gene gave a fine performance as Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gene' looks like an actor's first name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In genetics an inherited unit was once called a Mendelian element; a gene determines a heritable characteristic.

clue.text: Plot against American defecting is very easy initially

indicators.note: defecting says the American's letter leaves the word for against

parts.note: contra is Latin for against

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A conspiracy against an American who is defecting, which is very easy at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defecting' drops A from CONTRA; 'initially' gives IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot is to scheme or devise, to engineer something by cunning.

clue.text: Fruit is floating in torrent

indicators.note: floating in places the two letters inside the word for torrent, like something carried along in it

parts.note: heavy rain falls in torrents

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit drifts along in a fast-flowing stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a familiar dried fruit used in baking and snacks.

clue.text: Some claim pastoral style to lay it on thick

definitions.text: style to lay it on thick

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a claim about a rural painting style that piles on paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay it on thick' sounds like exaggeration but describes paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting technique applying paint in heavy layers so brushstrokes stand out is this style.

clue.text: Swallow's issue falls?

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
an issue is an outflow, a flowing out

explanation.surface: A bird's offspring tumble from the nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' and 'issue' read as a bird and its young but are the verbs down and flow; the question mark marks waterfalls as just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterfalls are an example of water travelling downward, a descending stream.

clue.text: Slog. Self-explanatory exits!

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer says take LOGS and send its S off round to the front, which spells Slog

explanation.surface: Hard work, it explains itself, and then everyone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as wordplay puts the last letter of LOGS off to the front, producing 'Slog'.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing out of a computer system is leaving it, so the phrasal verb means exits.

clue.text: Silver for one sanctimonious judge

parts.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A self-righteous judge awards silver.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver is Long John Silver of Treasure Island, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the buccaneer in Treasure Island, an example of a sea robber.

clue.text: Send home rogue pirate trapped by renegade European

indicators.note: trapped by puts the shuffled letters inside the surrounding letters

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts their side

indicators.note: rogue says the following letters go astray and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deserter from Europe catches a rogue pirate and has him deported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' gives the anagram EPATRI, 'trapped by' the deserter and European; a rat is a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To return someone to their native country is to send them back where they belong.

clue.text: Lacking precision, not very fit

indicators.note: not says the letter for very is to be left out

parts.note: something vague lacks precision

explanation.surface: Someone who is imprecise and not in good physical shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' reads as healthy but means a bout of fever.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit can be an attack of illness, and the word here names a malarial bout of fever and shivering.

clue.text: Healthy sounding salutation

indicators.note: sounding says the word for healthy is heard, not spelt

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A greeting that sounds healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting shouted to someone is a call of welcome, as in 'all hail'.

clue.text: Church division is impounding booze? On the contrary

indicators.note: impounding signals one piece held inside another
On the contrary reverses the roles, so the drink holds the two letters rather than the other way round

parts.note: ale is beer, informal booze

explanation.surface: A church congregation split over confiscating alcohol, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally IS would hold ALE; 'On the contrary' flips that, so ALE holds IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage or lateral section of a church, separated from the nave by pillars, is one of its divisions.

clue.text: Disney was one such man, to air figures in a new way

indicators.note: in a new way says the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Walt Disney was the kind of man to bring figures to life on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a new way' rearranges MAN TO AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney made cartoons, drawing figures that move on screen, so he was a cartoon film-maker of that kind.

clue.text: Fine little hoofer dances around hotel in fun

indicators.note: around has the rearranged letters surround the letter for hotel
dances says the letters jig about into a new order

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A small, excellent tap-dancer performs round a hotel just for amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' rearranges LITTLE HOOFER, which goes 'around' H, after F; a hoofer is slang for a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something just for amusement, with no other purpose, is the sense of the idiom.
